Every command here ran. Invented language ("Our language", qaa); paths, run ids, hashes, times and pids normalised. Made by scripts/rails_acceptance/record_demo.mjs; checked by its --check. Never edit by hand.

step.say: Bring in each file the person named, now, with add_data — from where it is (any path; never ask them to move it). Call it with just the path first: it reads the layout itself (a header naming the languages decides the columns) and asks only when it cannot tell — then ask the person what it asks. It reports counts and columns, never sentences.
step.why: A translation model learns from pairs. They stay on this computer; nothing is uploaded.
step.for_the_person: Bring in the sentence pairs you have — a spreadsheet (.xlsx, .ods, .csv), a .tsv or .txt, or a table in a Word document. Run `champollion data add <file>` with the file where it is (or drop it in inbox/ first); it asks which column is English and which is Our language when the header does not say. A word list (a dictionary) comes in the same way with `--into lexicon` — a Toolbox or LIFT (FieldWorks) dictionary too, whose example sentences can also come in as pairs. An ELAN (.eaf) file gives pairs from its transcription and translation tiers; grammar notes go in data/grammar/.

TEST ROWS WITH A NEAR-TWIN IN THE TRAINING DATA (what your test score will measure):
  project-test: 5 of 14 test rows (36%) have a near-twin in the training data — after training, the strict score on the other 9 rows is the generalization number (export reports it next to the full score)

An option, not a step: a model with no twin of any test row — for a test set that is a fixed, separate file, `nmt-forge leak-audit <corpus> --clean-to <corpus.notwins.jsonl> --drop-test-twins` drops the training rows that are near-twins (it says how many go) and writes that model's config; for a test set carved from your corpus, `nmt-forge split <corpus> --test N --dev M --seed S --out data/split --near-dupe 0.6` holds out whole templates

How to read this: overlap = shared words ÷ all words (Jaccard, diacritics folded); near-duplicates start at 60%. Exact = identical after case/punctuation/spacing normalization. Same corpus + same registered sets ⇒ the same result, every run.

step.say: Set aside 18 of the screened pairs as a dev set (the convention: one in ten, at least 50 — a quarter when there are fewer than 200 — at most 500; below 50 no round can be judged on them; seed 42 so it can be repeated) — the model is tuned on them, never on the test set, and rounds are judged on them. Near-copies (60% alike or more) stay on one side, so the dev set is not answered from memory — the same rule every later round's screen applies (groups are capped at 10, so a file written from templates still splits). A small dev set can only see big differences; it grows later from the speaker's practice sentences. To choose another size, run the command with your own --dev.

step.say: a training run is in progress: run 'qaa-nmt-cpu-tiny' (pid <n> on <host>, started <time>) — WAIT for it to finish. Do NOT start another run: two runs fight for the same CPU/GPU and memory, and `nmt-forge run` refuses while this one holds ~/family/.forge/run.lock. Run `nmt-forge status` again after the training process has exited (when you launched it in the background, wait on that process or its log — do not poll on a timer); status will then name the next step. Its run directory (checkpoints) is ~/family/.forge/runs/qaa-nmt-cpu-tiny-<hash>. It runs as background job train-<hash>-094245 (select); its supervisor stops it if it stalls or passes its deadline, and writes down why — `nmt-forge jobs` shows it.

a trained run exists — `export` decodes your test battery with the dev-selected checkpoint, scores it (prereg-gated, CI'd, with the Diagnosis), writes an mt-eval RunLog + TestReport into export/evaluation/ (your test sentences — never deployed), and packages the model you can serve into export/model/ — one step. A twin-free model is an option afterwards, not a step before: `nmt-forge leak-audit <training corpus> --clean-to <corpus>.notwins.jsonl --drop-test-twins`. This run's backend wrote no model weights, so the export is the evaluation only (--no-model): there is no model to serve from it.
